title: Fundament
goal: All cross-cutting services exist before any content: registry holders, config stat holders, combat (virtual health R4, 1.7.10 armor formula R5), per-player rider key state with payload and key mapping (R15), MyUtils with marker interfaces, the shared AI goals, world write helpers, a generic spawn egg with the five vanilla eggs, and client setup. The dedicated server starts. See docs/catalog/README.md section 4.2 and section 4.14 for back-edges (mark later-wave branches with // PORT: TODO Wxx).

workers.task: Registry holder classes per docs/STYLE.md (ModItems, ModBlocks, ModEntities, ModBlockEntities, ModMenus, ModCreativeTabs, ModAttachments, ModDataComponents - empty but wired, with init()); wire them and ModSounds in OreSpawn.java. Port the stat holders MobStats, ArmorStats, WeaponStats, OreStats as config/stats/ classes reading OreSpawnConfig at runtime and EarlyConfig for registration-time values, including every clamp the original applied after reading (see verhalten/core-01a.md and core-02.md). Port the lifecycle and global event handlers of OreSpawnMain that are not tied to content of a later wave (player events, tick handlers, login/chat messages, date checks per DECISIONS R18); content-specific branches become // PORT: TODO Wxx. Client setup class as successor of ClientProxyOreSpawn with empty registration hubs (EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterRenderers, RegisterLayerDefinitions, RegisterKeyMappingsEvent, RegisterClientExtensionsEvent) that later waves extend. Creative tabs as in the original (OreSpawnMain defines them). Write docs/port/W01.md in German listing the classes that are only ticked off and why: OreSpawnConstants (numeric ids, R2), OreSpawnSounds (generated ModSounds), CommonProxyOreSpawn (proxy pattern gone), EntityLavaLovingItem, PortalBlock, RockBlock, Slice, NightmareDungeon (dead code per behaviour chapters - verify in the source before ticking off).

Implement DECISIONS R4 and R5 from scratch (no original class). R4: virtual health - an interface or base helper that entities with original max health above 1024 implement; MAX_HEALTH attribute = min(original, 1024); incoming damage scaled by 1024/original after all original per-hit caps; boss bars stay correct. R5: the 1.7.10 armor formula damage*(25-armor)/25 (no cap, >=25 means no blockable damage) replacing the ARMOR reduction through NeoForge's DamageContainer in LivingIncomingDamageEvent - VERIFY the exact 1.21.1 API (DamageContainer, Reduction.ARMOR, addModifier) in the sources before writing; it applies when the target is an OreSpawn entity or a player wears at least one OreSpawn armor piece (use an item tag orespawn:legacy_armor that W03 fills, or an interface), armor sum computed from item defense values, not the clamped attribute. Respect isUnblockable-equivalent damage types (#minecraft:bypasses_armor). Add a small handwritten COMMON config config/PortConfig.java (own file name orespawn-port.toml) with legacyArmorFormula=true; registration goes through registry_entries into OreSpawn.java. Keep the math in plain static methods without Minecraft imports so the GameTest agent and unit tests can check the numbers.

Port KeyHandler, RiderControl, RiderControlMessage, RiderControlMessageHandler. Per DECISIONS R15 the fly-up key state is per player: a player AttachmentType (registration via registry_entries to ModAttachments), a C2S CustomPacketPayload registered in RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent, a KeyMapping registered in RegisterKeyMappingsEvent (verify the GLFW key for original key code 56, see catalogue README 6.3), sending only on state change like the original. Provide a static accessor (e.g. RiderKeys.isFlyUp(Player)) that later entities (Cephadrome, Dragon, Elevator, Leon, Ostrich, ThePrinceAdult, ThePrinceTeen) call instead of the old global flyup_keystate.

Port MyUtils: its predicates isRoyalty, isAttackableNonMob, isIgnoreable become three marker interfaces that later entities implement (catalogue README 4.1 point 1 - subclasses inherit them like the original instanceof checks); every other MyUtils helper ported 1:1. Port GenericTargetSorter, MyEntityAIWander and MyEntityAIWanderALot as 1.21.1 Goals/comparators with the original tick rates and chances. Add world write helpers replacing setBlockFast and setBlockIDWithMetadataInChunk for WorldGenLevel/Level (flags without neighbour updates where the original skipped them) for the worldgen waves.

Port ItemSpawnEgg and DispenserBehaviorOreSpawnEgg as ONE generic spawn egg item class taking a Supplier<EntityType>, per DECISIONS R9 (corrected): no DeferredSpawnEggItem, each egg keeps its own original icon texture via an item/generated model. Port the right-click and dispenser spawning behaviour 1:1 (including what the original does with enable flags - check the source). Register the five vanilla-mob eggs from the manifest (eggwitherskeleton, eggenderdragon, eggsnowgolem, eggirongolem, eggwitherboss) through registry_entries, and write their item model JSONs. Port the client renderers RenderInfo and RenderSpinner (spinner sprites from spinners.png) into client/renderer/ so later projectile waves can use RenderSpinner.

gametests: (1) the dedicated server starts and all W00 tests still pass; (2) virtual health: damage to an entity with original max health 7000 is scaled by 1024/7000 (if no OreSpawn entity exists yet, test the combat math and the event path on a vanilla entity through the same API); (3) legacy armor: with 25 armor points no blockable damage arrives, with 20 points 20% of it arrives, bypasses_armor damage is not reduced; (4) the five vanilla spawn eggs spawn their entity when used on a block; (5) the rider payload changes only the sending player's key state; (6) stat holders return the jar defaults (e.g. The King health 7000, Ultimate tool damage 36).
